title: Introduce attn-concierge kernel and continuous KV synchronizer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We continue to see tail latency and token-cost inefficiency for real-time small-batch workloads (chat UX and streaming). Previous kernel upgrades focused on bulk throughput; this change optimizes the hot path for small to medium sequence lengths while improving KV cache locality across continuous batching windows.

Summary of changes: Introduces a new "attn-concierge" microkernel and a runtime component called the Continuous KV Synchronizer. The concierge kernel consolidates small-op fusion: inline transposition for 64/128 heads, a compact rotary/rope fusion path that avoids extra re-layouts for common rotary sizes, and a shadow-prefetch lane that issues lightweight prefetches for K/V memory used by the next N micro-batches. The Continuous KV Synchronizer is a scheduling + background worker that keeps cold KV segments warm by re-registering frequently accessed KV ranges with the serving allocator and coordinating warmup I/O during idle gaps between continuous batches.

Key points: - Concierge kernel implements a fastpath for (seq_len <= 512, head_dim <= 128) with fused QK and rotary application to reduce memory traffic. - Shadow-prefetch lane is non-blocking and backpressure-aware; it can be disabled per-model via runtime flags. - KV Synchronizer uses a lightweight LRU+heatmap per-model to prioritize segments to warm; it integrates with existing KV eviction to avoid overcommit. - Scheduler hints: new per-request hint "kv_priority" that bumps KV synchronizer attention for critical/latency-sensitive routes. - New unit/driver tests + perf harness scenarios added to the benchmark-lab suite.

Design notes and motivations: Small-batch workloads suffered from repeated micro-transposes and redundant rotary multiplications when serving many short tokens. Prior solutions reduced kernel latency asymptotically but left a gap where memory movement dominated. By fusing steps commonly seen in our telemetry and adding a staged, cooperative prefetcher (shadow lane) we reduce per-token memory overhead while preserving numerics and FP16/FP32 accumulation paths. The KV synchronizer addresses the problem where continuous batching leaves KV shards cold when requests switch between lanes or models. Keeping these shards warm reduces first-token latency and avoids synchronous spill/reload windows that create latency spikes.

Testing and validation: - Perf microbenchmarks (benchmark-lab) show 8-14% median latency reduction and 18-30% improvement in token/sec for small clients (1-8 concurrent connections, seq_len 32–256) on T4/RTX6000-class hardware. - End-to-end chat demo workload shows 10% lower p99 in Canary traffic. - CI: added integration tests exercising scheduler hints and KV synchronizer toggles. - Safety: numeric parity tests for rotary/rope paths with 1e-6 tolerance.

Migration and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag "attn_concierge_enabled" and model annotation opt-in. Rollout plan: start with canary on Dedicated pools (low-rpm) -> expand to burst pools -> default on hosted after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.

Notes: This PR bundles kernel changes and small runtime pieces. Production toggle and observability hooks added (console metrics: concierge_hits, concierge_fallbacks, kv_sync_warmups).

- Introduce 'attn-concierge' microkernel for low-latency small-batch workloads
- Add Continuous KV Synchronizer to reduce first-token and cold-KV spikes
- New runtime flags and scheduler hints (attn_concierge_enabled, kv_priority)
- Observability metrics: concierge_hits, concierge_fallbacks, kv_sync_warmups
